academy.title: Learning Academy
academy.intro: Each module: outcomes, theory, demonstration, guided exercise, independent practice, knowledge quiz and practical assessment. Complete = all four steps, quiz and practical ≥ 80 %.
practice.note: No step-by-step guidance; hints on request.
practical.note: Hints disabled; scored from your simulator actions (offset accuracy, collisions, incorrect actions). Pass mark {pass} %.
dash.title: Learning Dashboard
dash.disclaimer: Independent educational simulator — not an official Haas Automation product. Scores reflect simulated actions only.
assess.title: Competency Assessment
assess.intro: Scores come from the simulator state you produce (offset accuracy, setup, completion) plus recorded collisions, incorrect actions, alarms, hints and time — not from button clicks alone. Practice and independent assessments randomise tool lengths and workpiece positions (seed shown in the result). Guided assessment keeps fixed parameters and step guidance.
lesson.metrics: Correct operations {ok} · incorrect {bad} · collisions {coll} · alarms {al} · hints {h} · time {t} s
lesson.simWarn: Simulator practice only — real machine training must be supervised.
ctrl.keysNote: Controller keys and screens stay in English, as on the Haas control.
cases.title: Industrial case studies
cases.intro: Six synthetic scenarios built only from the lessons and controls this simulator has. Each one lists objectives, a procedure, acceptance checks and the mistakes that usually cost marks.
cases.contentNote: The procedure, acceptance checks and pitfalls stay in English because they use Haas technical wording.
ref.title: Technical reference
ref.intro: Facts recorded in this project's source register: the Haas mill manual, the UMC supplement and the UMC-500 layout drawing. Anything not verified is listed separately instead of being presented as machine truth.
ref.contentNote: Technical terms stay in English, as on the Haas control and in the manuals.
guide.title: User guide
guide.intro: How to use Haas Virtual Lab: learning modes, the academy, the dashboard and its exports, case studies, keyboard shortcuts and the limits of the simulation.
guide.start.s: Open the simulator to explore the machine, or the academy for the staged path M01–M12. Progress is stored in this browser, so you can close the tab and continue later.
guide.modes.s: Guided shows every step and why it matters. Practice hides the answers and scores the actions you take. Assessment generates a randomised variant that is scored the same way.
guide.academy.s: Each module has outcomes, sourced theory, a demonstration, guided steps, a practice exercise and a quiz. Modules M07 (probing), M11 (programs) and M12 (full workflow) stay unavailable until Phases 4 and 6 are implemented.
guide.dashboard.s: The dashboard shows overall progress, competency by category, common mistakes, revision suggestions and every attempt. It exports CSV, a JSON backup (restorable) and a printable report.
guide.cases.s: Case studies combine the lessons into a realistic synthetic job, with acceptance checks. The reference lists source documents, control keys, travels, simulated commands, a glossary and everything still unverified.
guide.shortcuts.s: Every control is a real button reachable with Tab and Enter. In the simulator the arrow keys jog the selected axis, PageUp/PageDown jog Y, and the divider between machine and controller is resizable from the keyboard.
guide.data.s: There is no server and no account. Progress, language and display settings live in this browser's local storage; export a JSON backup to move them to another machine, and reset them from the dashboard or settings.
guide.limits.s: This is an educational simulator, not machine control. Unverified machine data is flagged in the reference. Real machine training must be supervised and follows the manufacturer's manuals.

case.CS-1.title: First plate in a vice
case.CS-1.scenario: A 80 × 60 × 20 mm aluminium plate must be set up with G54 at the top-left corner. The tools are already in the library and nothing is clamped yet.
case.CS-1.objectives: Seat the plate on parallels and clamp it without tilting the datum
Touch off X, Y and Z for G54 with the mounted tool
Prove the datum with a clearance move before any cutting
case.CS-2.title: Centre datum with an edge finder
case.CS-2.scenario: A 100 mm round bar sits in the vice and the drawing dimensions everything from its centre. The datum must be the bar centre, not an edge.
case.CS-2.objectives: Find X and Y with the edge finder and apply the radius correction once
Set Z on the top face with a gauge block for the reference tool
Confirm the centre datum from both directions
case.CS-3.title: Two parts, two offsets
case.CS-3.scenario: Two identical blanks sit side by side on the platter. The job needs G54 for part A and G55 for part B, without disturbing either setup.
case.CS-3.objectives: Build two independent work offsets from measured positions
Switch between G54 and G55 and read the resulting coordinates
Show that setting one offset leaves the other untouched
case.CS-4.title: 3+2 bracket on the trunnion
case.CS-4.scenario: A bracket needs three faces machined. It is clamped on the platter and positioned with B45 C120 for the first face, then re-oriented for the others.
case.CS-4.objectives: Rotate to a 3+2 orientation without sweeping the part through the vice
Position with DWO active and explain what DWO changes
Cancel the rotary mode correctly before jogging
case.CS-5.title: Recover from an E-stop mid-setup
case.CS-5.scenario: An E-stop is pressed while jogging during a setup. The part, tool and offsets already measured must survive the recovery.
case.CS-5.objectives: Reach a safe state and clear the alarm in the documented order
Show that measured offsets are not lost by the E-stop
case.CS-6.title: Prove the setup before cutting
case.CS-6.scenario: A colleague hands over a prepared machine with no notes. Before cutting, the setup has to be diagnosed and the result recorded for the supervisor.
case.CS-6.objectives: Find an incorrect work offset from the coordinate evidence
Diagnose a tool-length plus work-offset mistake
Record the outcome as an exported assessment report
